context_requirements: Active cAMP/PKA signaling or dependence on PKA-driven survival/proliferation
Intact apoptotic machinery for secondary cell death effects
PKA-dependent regulation of target genes such as CREB1, CCND1, MYC
falsifiers: No change in CREB1, FOS, JUN, or EGR1 at 6 h in any responsive line
No decrease in CCND1, MYC, or BCL2 at 24 h
No antiproliferative or apoptotic gene signature at 24 h
Uniform strong responses across all nine lines including those with low PKA activity

evidence.supports: H-89 is a selective PKA inhibitor, confirming PRKACA as a direct target
H89 and KT5720 ablate PKA-dependent survival, linking PKA inhibition to apoptosis
H89 synergizes with oncolytic virus via Epac1 and ER stress, suggesting context-dependent effects
H89 modulates BDNF, Bcl2, and AKT in neuronal cells, indicating PKA-dependent survival signaling

changes: Moved CREB1, FOS, JUN, and EGR1 from proximal_up to proximal_down: PKA inhibition reduces CREB phosphorylation and lowers transcription of these immediate-early genes.
Kept PCK2 in proximal_up: PKA inhibition relieves cAMP-mediated repression of PCK2, consistent with gluconeogenic gene induction.

Removed generic proliferation/stress genes from proximal lists: CCND1, MYC, BCL2, BIRC5, MMP1, MMP2, HIF1A, SERPINE1, PTGS2 are secondary or generic and were moved to proximal_down only where direction is justified.
No gene appears in both up and down lists at the same time.
